title: בן סבר

paragraphs:
Ben Sevar pursued charity throughout his life. Once he heard of an orphan in a nearby province wishing to marry, lacking the means. He took everything at home and gave it to him. Returning, he met a river four parasangs long with a tannin harming every passerby. When he reached it, it made itself a bridge; he crossed unharmed. Beyond the river an exceedingly ugly man asked if he was Ben Sevar, where he had come from, and heard everything. The man said, “I have your ledger. Your time to depart this world has come.” Ben Sevar turned pale and appealed to Heaven: should one devoted to Torah and kindness die young—this Torah and this reward? Outside his dwelling like an animal, without his household tending him? A heavenly voice granted time until he reached his bed.

Leaving the Angel of Death, he met people leaving a town and asked for a great sage or student to greet. They named Shefifon ben Layish. Shefifon welcomed him joyfully but saw his pale face, asking whether he needed bread or anything. Ben Sevar lacked nothing. Asked why pale, he told his journey. Shefifon promised God's rescue from death. After five days a great cloud surrounded the house. His students asked about it; he told them to see whether it surrounded the town or only the house. The Angel of Death demanded his deposit: Shefifon's life and Ben Sevar's. Shefifon dismissed him to his work; he held nothing for him. The angel reported that Shefifon barred entry, adjuring him by God's great name. God said, “Go tell him: By your life, I ask only for Ben Sevar’s life.” He returned with that message; Shefifon answered as before. A heavenly voice asked what to do with these two righteous men: decrees could not be fulfilled. 'You shall decree a thing and it will be established'; 'A righteous one rules in God's fear.' Who rules Me? A righteous person: I decree and he annuls it; for him I annul it. He told them to add seventy years to each one's life. Sefer Katan Ma'asiyyot. See Yehudah HaSabbar; perhaps this is he.
